0.value:
llm_layout shows a language model writing, as a picture, token by token.

IT TAKES COMMANDS, NOT TEXT:
Wire gemma_4's 'layout_out' to its 'input' (qwen_moe and bonsai_2 have the same outlet). That outlet does not send text - it sends COMMANDS, and this node is what understands them:

add <id> <token> <value>    another token, coloured by the value
prompt <id> <token>         a token of the prompt, in white
streaming_prompt / accept_streamed_prompt / backspace_streaming_prompt
                            a prompt being typed in live
choice_list / choose        the alternatives the model weighed, and which
                            one was picked
step_back <n>               take back the last n tokens
temperature / show_probs    display settings changing
scroll_up / scroll_down     move active_line by one
clear / reset               empty it
save                        write the text to llama_output_<date>.txt in
                            the folder the app was started from

So the two nodes together give you a screen that shows the model writing, including the parts a plain text display cannot show: which alternatives it was considering, and which one was chosen.

The picture is 1920 by 1080, three channels, as floats from 0 to 1, laid out height-first like a camera frame, in the Inconsolata font.

'active_line' IS WHY IT READS WELL:
New text always appears on the same line of the screen - line 17 by default - and everything above scrolls up as it fills. The writing happens at a fixed height rather than creeping down the page, which is far easier to read and to point a camera at.

When the model's 'show_probs' is switched on, the node moves it up to line 5, so there is room below for the list of alternatives, and back to 17 when it is switched off. That is worth knowing so it does not look like a fault when the text jumps.

'colour_mode' SHOWS THE MODEL'S UNCERTAINTY:
Each 'add' carries a value, and the token is coloured by it - so the text carries how sure the model was as it wrote. Which value is sent is set on the model ('display_mode' on gemma_4): its temperature, the entropy, or the probability of the token. 'colour_mode' here picks the colour scale to read it with, and should match.

'include prompt' decides whether 'prompt' tokens - what you asked - are shown along with the answer.

SYNTAX:
llm_layout

EXAMPLE:
llm_layout

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

input:
The layout commands.

clear:
Empty it.

active_line:
Which line of the screen new text appears on, 17.

colour_mode:
temperature, entropy or probability - the scale for each token's value.

include prompt:
Show the prompt as well as the answer.

OUTPUTS:

layout:
The rendered image.

RELATED:
gemma_4, qwen_moe and bonsai_2, whose 'layout_out' this is built to receive. cairo_layout for plain text as a picture; llm_layout used to share its page. mgl_texture or gl nodes to get the image onto a screen.
